q1_issues.issue: The Name string carries the appositive party-and-state tag ('Sen. John Rockefeller, D-W.Va.'); the title rule licenses keeping 'Sen.' in the string, but 'D-W.Va.' is an appositive outside the name, and its content (Democrat, West Virginia) is dropped rather than encoded.

q2_gaps: abbreviated party-and-state appositive on a legislator's name ('D-W.Va.') - neither a courtesy title nor a full appositive NP, so no licensed encoding
proper-noun modifier of a common noun denoting affiliation - 'the Senate bill'
notes: Sealing is handled well: the non-factive 'say' complement asserts nothing at top level, the definite provision and bill typings project while the indefinite 'a basic tenet' keeps its typing inside the seal, and 'basic' is correctly left unfused as incidental description. Reading 'that' as a complementizer rather than a demonstrative determiner is not a defect here, since both readings yield the same atoms.
